chunks: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) saying: When the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) saw Taym, ʿAdiyy, and Banī Umayyah ascending his pulpit, it horrified him. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down Qur'an by which he would be consoled:
And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' so they prostrated except Iblīs; he refused.
Then He revealed to him: O Muḥammad, I commanded but was not obeyed, so do not grieve if you command and are not obeyed concerning your successor.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam cited as the speaker in the report
key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblīs, who refused the command to prostrate
key_terms.اسْجُدُوا: prostrate, the divine command given to the angels
key_terms.قُرْآنًا: Qur'an, revealed here as a source of consolation
key_terms.مِنْبَرَهُ: his pulpit, symbolizing the Prophet’s authority and position
key_terms.وَصِيِّكَ: your successor, the one designated after you

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Prophet’s grief over opposition to his appointed successor?
ai.summary: This narration presents the Prophet's grief upon seeing certain clans ascend his pulpit and explains that Allah consoled him through the example of Iblīs refusing a divine command. Its significance is in framing disobedience to the Prophet regarding his وصيّ as part of a broader pattern of refusal against divinely mandated authority.
